title: Finite normalization of a generically smooth curve over a separably closed valuation base
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-weil-field, def-kun-separably-closed] and $V\subseteq K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for every $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ belongs to $V$. Assume the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain. Put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], flat and finitely presented over $T$ [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with all nonempty fibres pure of topological Krull dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and with smooth generic fibre [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Pure dimension one means that every irreducible component has dimension one. Then the normalization $n:X^\nu\to X$ in its function field [def-sc-normalization] is finite and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], is an isomorphism on the generic fibre, and $X^\nu$ is normal, flat and finitely presented over $T$ with all nonempty fibres pure of dimension one. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring].

source.place: Section 4.1, opening paragraph, printed p. 25: finiteness and finite presentation of normalization from Theorem 3.5.5 and Proposition 3.5.2; smooth-generic-fibre case of this normalization assertion. Primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The valuation ring $V$ and each $V_{\mathfrak p}$ are integrally closed: if $z$ in the fraction field is integral but outside a valuation ring, then $z^{-1}$ belongs to its maximal ideal; dividing a monic equation for $z$ by its leading power puts $1$ in that ideal, a contradiction. Thus $T$ is normal integral qcqs. Apply [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free] with $L=\mathcal O_X$ to each nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$. Every nonzero element of $V$ acts injectively on $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], its generic fibre has ring $A_K=(V\setminus0)^{-1}A$. This is a nonzero domain and $A\hookrightarrow A_K$ is injective. Consequently the generic fibre is nonempty, integral, and dense in $X$: a section vanishing on it vanishes in each affine ring, and each nonempty basic affine open has nonzero generic localization. In particular $X\to T$ is dominant.

source.place: §4.1 opening paragraph, printed p. 25; agent expansion of Theorem 3.5.5 and Proposition 3.5.2

proof.text: The smooth curve $X_\eta$ is normal by [lem-sc-smooth-normal] and geometrically reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. Its dimension is one by the hypothesis on fibres. Apply [lem-trf-reduced-fibre-modification] to $X\to T$, using integrality and qcqs of $T$, dominance from step 1, finite presentation from the hypothesis, and this geometric reducedness. Obtain $r:T\prime\to T$ and $q:Y\prime\to X\times_TT\prime$, with $Y\prime$ flat finitely presented over $T\prime$ and with reduced geometric fibres. The generic fibre of $r$ is $\operatorname{Spec}L$ for a finite separable extension $L/K$. By [def-kun-separably-closed], this extension is $K$ itself.

source.place: §4.1 opening paragraph, printed p. 25; agent expansion of Theorem 3.5.5 and Proposition 3.5.2

proof.text: The generic point $\operatorname{Spec}K\to T\prime$ extends to a section $\sigma:T\to T\prime$ by [lemma-nagata-proper-valuative-criterion-existence-api], since $r$ is proper and $V$ is a valuation ring with fraction field $K$. Pull back $q$ along $X\to X\times_T T\prime$ induced by $\sigma$, obtaining $Y=Y\prime\times_{T\prime}T$ and $h:Y\to X$. This map is finite: on affine charts it is the tensor base change of a finite algebra, and the tensors of a finite module generating set still generate. Its generic fibre is the identity of $X_\eta$ by the generic-fibre isomorphism of $q$. The map $Y\to T$ is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), flat by [lem-pc-relatively-flat-module-pullback] applied to $\mathcal O_{Y\prime}$ (its pullback is $\mathcal O_Y$), and has reduced geometric fibres by [lem-trf-geometric-reduced-fibre-locus-base-change].

source.place: §4.1 opening paragraph, printed p. 25; agent expansion of Theorem 3.5.5 and Proposition 3.5.2

proof.text: For each nonempty affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset Y$, apply [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free] with $L=\mathcal O_U$ and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change]. Then $B\hookrightarrow B_K$ and $B_K\ne0$. The scheme $U_K$ is a nonempty affine open in $Y_K=X_\eta$, which is integral, so $B_K$ and hence $B$ are domains. The generic fibre meets every nonempty open of $Y$ by the same localization argument. Since $Y_K$ is irreducible, any two nonempty opens of $Y$ meet; thus $Y$ is integral and $Y_K$ is dense. Each such $U\to T$ is flat, has reduced geometric fibres, and is finitely presented: its map is locally of finite presentation by restriction, and affine $U$ and affine $T$ supply the qcqs hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). Apply [lem-trf-geometrically-reduced-eta-normal] to $U\to T$. It says every finite eta-modification of $U$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: §4.1 opening paragraph, printed p. 25; agent expansion of Theorem 3.5.5 and Proposition 3.5.2

proof.text: We now show directly that the affine domain $B$ of step 4 is integrally closed. Let $b\in\operatorname{Frac}B$ be integral over $B$. Its image is integral over $B_K$; this ring is normal, since $U_K$ is an open of the normal smooth curve $X_\eta$. More explicitly a rational integral element lies in every normal local ring of $U_K$, and its local regular representatives agree in the function field and glue to a section. Therefore $b\in B_K$, so $b=c/a$ for $c\in B$ and $a\in V\setminus0$. The algebra $B[b]$ is finite over $B$, generated as a module by $1,b,\ldots,b^{m-1}$ for a monic equation of degree $m$. Its spectrum is proper over $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. It is an isomorphism on $D(a)$ and on the generic fibre. Both rings are subrings of $\operatorname{Frac}B$, so $a$ acts injectively on their localizations; hence these $D(a)$ opens are schematically dense. This is a finite eta-modification of $U$, so step 4 makes it an isomorphism. Thus $b\in B$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization], applied to $B\subset\operatorname{Frac}B$, shows that every $B_{\mathfrak p}$ is integrally closed. Hence $Y$ is normal.

source.place: §4.1 opening paragraph, printed p. 25; agent expansion of Theorem 3.5.5 and Proposition 3.5.2

proof.text: Identify $h$ with the normalization. For any nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$, its preimage is $\operatorname{Spec}B$, with $B$ finite over $A$. It is nonempty because its generic fibre is that of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. The generic-fibre isomorphism and integrality from steps 1 and 4 identify their fraction fields with $k(X)$ and embed $A\subset B\subset k(X)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], $B$ lies in the integral closure $\overline A$ of $A$ in $k(X)$. Conversely every $z\in\overline A$ satisfies a monic equation over $A\subset B$, so normality of $B$ from step 5 implies $z\in B$. Thus $B=\overline A$. These identifications agree on restrictions, as they are inclusions into the same function field; alternatively [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization] gives this on principal opens. The definition [def-sc-normalization] therefore identifies $Y$ over $X$ with $X^\nu$. Consequently $n$ is finite, is an isomorphism on the generic fibre, and its source is normal, flat and finitely presented over $T$.

source.place: §4.1 opening paragraph, printed p. 25; agent expansion of Theorem 3.5.5 and Proposition 3.5.2

proof.text: The finite map $n$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], so its image is closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The image contains the dense generic fibre of $X$; hence it is all of $X$. Finally $X^\nu\to T$ is flat and finitely presented, hence locally of finite type, and its generic fibre is the dense pure dimension-one curve $X_\eta$ by steps 2--4. Apply [lem-trf-flat-dense-generic-fibre-pure-dimension] with $d=1$ to get that every nonempty fibre of $X^\nu$ is pure of dimension one. Empty fibres impose no condition.
